hints.title: Parity Invariance Property
hints.text: Notice that 2 * A[k] is always even. If one element is odd and the other is even, their sum is odd and can never equal 2 * A[k].

hints.title: Odd and Even Subproblem Partition
hints.text: Partition elements into odd numbers and even numbers. If all odds appear before all evens, no cross pair can ever violate the arithmetic progression property.

hints.title: Divide and Conquer Scaling
hints.text: Apply divide and conquer recursively. Map an existing beautiful array of size ceil(n/2) via 2*x - 1 to form the odd portion, and map a beautiful array of size floor(n/2) via 2*x to form the even portion. Concatenate both.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all permutations and validating the arithmetic progression condition takes O(N! * N^2) time, which is impossible for N up to 1000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Doubling the array size iteratively at each step reaches or exceeds N in log2(N) steps, spending O(N) work per level.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should spot the odd-even parity invariance: odd + even is never an even number (2 * middle).
complexity.notes: Filtering elements <= n from the final doubled array produces the exact permutation of 1 to n.
